Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה - פליג אדלעיל, דקתני שנדו את עקביא:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda - [He] disagrees with what was stated above, which taught that they excommunicated Akavya.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:2.hebrew: שאין עזרה ננעלת - בפרק ה' דפסחים (דף סד:), שהיו שערי העזרה ננעלים כששוחטין פסחים של כל כת וכת, שהפסח נשחט בג' כתות:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:2.english: For the [Temple] Courtyard is not locked - [This is explained] in chapter 5 of Pesachim (folio 64b): that the gates of the Courtyard would be locked when they slaughtered the Pesach-offerings of each and every group, as the Pesach-offering was slaughtered in three groups.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:3.hebrew: על כל אדם בישראל - כלומר, כשהיתה ננעלת עליהם — והיינו כשנתמלאה פה לפה — לא היה בכולם אדם חשוב בחכמה ויראת חטא כעקביא:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:3.english: Upon any person in Israel - That is to say, when it [the Courtyard] was locked upon them — that is, when it was filled to capacity — there was not among all of them a person as distinguished in wisdom and fear of sin as Akavya.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:4.hebrew: אלעזר בן חנוך שפקפק - זילזל, והיינו נמי לכבוד הרב, שעבר ע"פ הגוזרים על הידים:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:10:4.english: Elazar ben Ḥanokh who doubted - [He] demeaned [it]. And this, too, is for the honor of the Master, for he transgressed the word of those who decreed concerning the [washing of] hands.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:1.hebrew: אלמלא חוני אתה - שיצא שמך בגדולה ובחשיבות:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:1.english: If you were not Ḥoni - For your name has become renowned for greatness and importance.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:2.hebrew: צריך אתה להתנדות - לפי שהטריח לפני המקום על עסק גשמים, "לא כך שאלתי" כמה פעמים. וכבוד המקום — כבוד הרב הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:2.english: You deserve to be excommunicated - Because he troubled the Omnipresent regarding the matter of rain, [saying,] "Not like this did I ask," several times; and the honor of the Omnipresent is the honor of the Master.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:3.hebrew: מתחטא - לשון חוטא — נקל בלבו לחטוא לאביו, ולהטריחו על תאותו:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:11:3.english: Acts petulantly - [This is] an expression of sinning [ḥotei]: it is a light matter in his heart to sin against his father and to trouble him for his desire.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:1.hebrew: מקולסים - צלויים כשהן שלמין, ותולין כרעיהן וקרסוליהן וקרביהם סביבותן בשפוד. ועל שם כך קורהו מקולס, שהוא לשון מזויין, כדמתרגם וכובע נחושת על ראשו (שמואל א י״ז:ה׳) — וקולסא דנחשא:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:1.english: Helmeted [kids] - [They are] roasted while they are whole, and they hang their legs, their ankles, and their entrails around them on the spit. And on account of this, it calls it "helmeted" [mekulas], which is an expression of being armed, as [the Targum] translates: "And a helmet of bronze was upon his head" (I Samuel 17:5) — "and a helmet [kolsa] of bronze."

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:2.hebrew: בלילי פסחים - זכר לפסח, שצולהו שלם, שנאמר בו: על כרעיו ועל קרבו (שמות י״ב:ט׳) — כלומר: עם כרעיו ועם קרבו:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:2.english: On the nights of Passover - In commemoration of the Paschal offering, which one roasts whole, as it is stated regarding it: "upon its legs and upon its entrails" (Exodus 12:9) — that is to say, with its legs and with its entrails.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:3.hebrew: גוזרני עליך נדוי - והיינו נמי לכבוד הרב, שאסרו חכמים את הדבר, לפי שהוא קרוב להאכיל את ישראל קדשים בחוץ, שהרואה סבור שהקדישו לשם פסח:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:12:3.english: I would decree excommunication upon you - And this, too, is for the honor of the Master: for the Sages forbade this matter, because it is akin to feeding Israel consecrated [meat] outside [the Temple], as an onlooker assumes that he consecrated it for the sake of the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:14:1.hebrew: חתכו חוליות - תנור של חרס, שהוא עשוי ככלי ומטלטל, ותחלת ברייתו מן הטיט ומצרפו בכבשן כשאר קדרות, ואם נטמא, הצריכו הכתוב נתיצה. ואם נתצו בענין זה — שחתכו סביב סביב כחוליות עגולות, וחזר וחיברו בטיט של חול בין חוליא לחוליא — רבי אליעזר מטהר עולמית, שאינו עוד ככלי חרס, שלא נשרף בכבשן; וחכמים מטמאין:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:14:1.english: [If] he cut it into segments - [This refers to] an earthenware oven, which is made as a vessel and is portable, and its initial creation is from clay and one fires it in a kiln like other earthenware pots; and if it became impure, Scripture required its demolition. And if he demolished it in this manner — that he cut it all around like circular rings, and then rejoined it with sandy mortar between each ring — Rabbi Eliezer deems [it] permanently pure, for it is no longer [considered] an earthenware vessel, since it was not fired in a kiln; and the Sages deem [it] impure.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:14:2.hebrew: כעכנאי - כנחש זה שכורך עצמו בעגולה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:14:2.english: Like an akhnai - Like this snake that coils itself in a circle.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:16:1.hebrew: כל טהרות - שנעשו בתנור זה, או שנגעו באוירו, והיה רבי אליעזר מטהרן, והם שרפום:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:16:1.english: All the ritually pure items - That were made in this oven or touched its airspace, and Rabbi Eliezer had declared them pure, and they [the Sages] burned them.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:16:2.hebrew: וברכוהו - לפי שהרבה מאד לחלוק בדבר זה, כדאמרינן בבבא מציעא בפרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף נט:):
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:16:2.english: And they “blessed” him - Because he disputed exceedingly concerning this matter, as we say in Bava Metzia in chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 59b).

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:17:1.hebrew: נדוי במתני' לא תנן - הא דברכוהו, בברייתא הוא דתני לה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:17:1.english: We did not learn [of] excommunication in the mishna - That [fact] that they “blessed” [i.e., excommunicated] him is taught in a baraita.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:17:2.hebrew: מדמה מילתא למילתא - כל מקום שראה במתניתין שנחלק היחיד על הרבים מחלוקת גדולה, או אחד מן החכמים שמדבר קשה כנגד גדול הימנו, אומר: ראוי היה כאן נדוי:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:17:2.english: Likens one matter to another - Wherever he saw in the Mishnah that an individual disagreed with the majority in a major dispute, or one of the Sages spoke harshly against someone greater than himself, he says: "Excommunication was warranted here."

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:18:1.english: They do not take out the deceased - To bury him.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:18:2.hebrew: סמוך לקריאת שמע - לפי שמתבטלין מן הקריאה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:18:2.english: Close to the recitation of Shema - Because they will be prevented from the recitation.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:19:1.hebrew: אין המת מוטל לפניהם - שהמת בבית אחר, והם מספידין אותו כאן. ויש מפרשין שנתון לצד אחר:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:19:1.english: [If] the deceased is not laid out before them - That the deceased is in another house, and they are eulogizing him here. And some explain that he is placed to another side.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:19:2.english: And he sits and remains silent - [This refers to] the mourner.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:1:1.hebrew: ואי ס"ד דלא ידעי - אין מבינין כלום, אלא צערא דגופא:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:1:1.english: And if it should enter your mind that they do not know - They understand nothing except the pain of the body.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:20:1.hebrew: למימר הכי - לא נפרעת ממני, דמשמע: הפרע:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:20:1.english: To say this - [Namely,] "You have not exacted payment from me," as it implies: "Exact payment!"

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:2:1.hebrew: המספר אחר המת - בגנותו של מת אחר מיתתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:2:1.english: One who speaks after the deceased - [Speaking] disparagingly of the deceased after his death.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:3:1.hebrew: קניא מטללא - קנה גדול וכבד נפל מן הגג:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:3:1.english: A reed from the roof - A large and heavy reed fell from the roof.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:3:3.hebrew: ארנקא דמוחיה - כיס שהמוח מונח בו:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:3:3.english: The pouch of his brain - The pouch in which the brain rests.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:5:1.hebrew: והמטים עקלקלותם - לעיל מיניה כתיב ״הטיבה ה' לטובים״, וסמיך ליה ״והמטים עקלקלותם״ — והמכריעים את חובותם יותר על זכיותם, להטותם לכף חובה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:5:1.english: And those who turn aside to their crooked ways - Earlier in [the psalm] it is written: “Do good, O Lord, to the good,” and adjacent to it: “And those who turn aside to their crooked ways” — [meaning,] those who tip the balance of their sins to outweigh their merits, so as to tilt them toward the scale of guilt.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:5:2.english: The Lord will lead them away with the workers of iniquity - To Gehenna.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:7:1.hebrew: בכ"ד מקומות - השתא משמע — מצינו שנדו חכמים בני אדם בכ"ד מקומות לכבוד הרב, לפי שלא נשאו כבוד לרבם:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:7:1.english: In twenty-four places - At this stage, it implies that we find that the Sages ostracized people in twenty-four places for the honor of the master, because they did not show respect to their master.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:1.hebrew: הוא היה אומר - עקביא בן מהללאל במסכת עדיות:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:1.english: He would say - [This refers to] Akavya ben Mahalalel in Tractate Eduyot.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:2.hebrew: אין משקין - אם קינא לה בעלה ונסתרה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:2.english: They do not make [her] drink - If her husband warned her and she secluded herself.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:3.hebrew: לא את הגיורת - דבני ישראל אמור בפרשה (במדבר ה), פרט לאשת גר ועבד משוחרר:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:3.english: Neither a female convert - For "Children of Israel" is stated in the passage (Numbers 5), excluding the wife of a convert and [the wife of] an emancipated slave.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:4.hebrew: בכרכמית - כך שמה, או על שם מקומה:
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:4.english: In [the case of] Kharkemit - That was her name, or [she was named] after her place.

Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:5.hebrew: דוגמא השקוה - על שהיו דומים להם, הם השקוה — שהיו שמעיה ואבטליון מבני בניו של סנחריב, כדאמרינן בגיטין בפרק הנזקין (גיטין דף נז:):
Rashi on Berakhot 19a:9:5.english: They made her drink [as someone] like them - Because they were similar to them, they made her drink, for Shemaya and Avtalyon were descendants of Sennacherib, as we say in Gittin in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 57b).

Tosafot on Berakhot 19a:5:1.hebrew: אפי' בשעה ששלום על ישראל - והיינו לאחר מיתתו, דלא אתו לאנצויי בהדי המספרים בגנותם. מהכא משמע דאיירי לאחר מיתה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 19a:5:1.english: "Even at a time when there is peace upon Israel" - And this refers to after his death, as they [the deceased] do not come to quarrel with those who speak disparagingly of them. From here it is implied that [the statement] is dealing with [speaking ill] after death.

Tosafot on Berakhot 19a:9:1.hebrew: דוגמא השקוה - פרש"י: לפי שהיתה גיורת כמותם, שהיו גרים. וכן משמע בירושלמי דמועד קטן (פ"ג): "מהו דוגמא? דכוות'". בערוך פירש: "דוגמא השקוה" — מי צבע, אבל לא היו מרים ממש, ולא מחקו התורה עליה, אלא ליראה אותה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 19a:9:1.english: "They made her drink dugma" - Rashi explains: Because she was a convert like them, as they were converts. And so it is implied in the Yerushalmi in Moed Katan (chapter 3): "What is dugma? [One] like her." In the Arukh, he explains: "They made her drink dugma" — [meaning] colored water, but they were not actual bitter waters, and they did not erase the Torah for her, but rather [only] to frighten her.
